metadata.title: Schema and Contract Governance

props.name: capability
props.remarks: Business capability for governing the semantic structure, evolution, and interpretation of messages exchanged through integrations.

props.name: technology-domain
props.remarks: Message schemas, contracts, validation rules, and schema lifecycle management systems.

props.name: architecture-pattern
props.remarks: Supporting pattern defining semantic trust and contract governance without implying authorization or business intent.

props.name: data-pattern
props.remarks: Defines schemas and contracts as semantic control data governing interpretation, not as permission or entitlement.

props.name: nist-guidance
props.remarks: Controls governing data integrity, validation, and system interconnections (SI, PL, SA families).

props.name: nist-guidance
props.remarks: Zero Trust guidance asserting that structurally valid data does not imply authorization, correctness, or intent.

props.name: nist-guidance
props.remarks: Guidance for auditing schema enforcement, validation failures, and contract violations.

metadata.remarks: Schema and Contract Governance defines how message structure and semantics are governed to prevent misinterpretation and semantic over‑trust. This pattern does not authorize business actions, imply correctness of outcomes, or enforce delivery or replay semantics.

components.title: Schema Definition and Ownership
components.description: Explicit definition of message schemas and assignment of ownership and accountability.

props.name: attack-technique
props.remarks: Manipulation of data structure to induce incorrect interpretation.

props.name: defense-technique
props.remarks: Explicit schema ownership prevents unauthorized semantic change.

implemented-requirements.remarks: Data structure ownership and governance responsibilities are formally defined.

components.title: Schema Validation
components.description: Validation of messages against approved schemas or contracts prior to processing.

props.name: attack-technique
props.remarks: Use of malformed or unexpected structures to bypass processing logic.

props.name: defense-technique
props.remarks: Schema validation enforces semantic correctness boundaries.

implemented-requirements.remarks: Input validation checks ensure messages conform to expected structure.

components.title: Contract Compatibility Governance
components.description: Governance of backward and forward compatibility to prevent consumer breakage or semantic drift.

props.name: defense-technique
props.remarks: Compatibility rules prevent implicit contract changes.

implemented-requirements.remarks: Interface changes are governed to prevent unintended downstream effects.

components.title: Schema Non‑Equivalence Constraints
components.description: Explicitly defines what schema validity does not grant or imply.

implemented-requirements.remarks: Schema conformance does not imply authorization, correctness, or approval of resulting actions.
